Starting state: Ardour installed; profile not yet applied
Steps: Apply profile; create new session; choose Beat Production template.
Expected result: Session opens with audio/MIDI tracks, A Reverb, B Delay and Master; transport is ready.
Pass criterion: Complete without consulting Ardour-native terminology docs.

Scenario: Navigate the workspace by muscle memory
Steps: Press Tab twice; press Shift+Tab twice; focus Browser; return to timeline.
Expected result: Arrangement/Session and Clip/Devices toggles are deterministic and focus remains visible.
Pass criterion: No unintended rename, text focus or transport action.

Steps: Open/focus Browser; search instrument; press Enter; play MIDI input.
Expected result: Instrument is inserted on the selected track and sound is produced.
Pass criterion: No modal plugin search beyond the unified browser target experience.

Steps: Create MIDI clip; open lower editor; draw notes; quantize; edit velocity; loop.
Expected result: A synchronized eight-bar MIDI part plays with edited velocity.
Pass criterion: User completes using proposed shortcuts with at most one tooltip lookup.
Evidence to capture: MIDI region; shortcut log; completion time

Scenario: Import and arrange an audio loop
Steps: Drag a WAV loop to Arrangement; trim; duplicate; consolidate; set loop.
Expected result: Loop is arranged non-destructively and repeats over the selected span.
Pass criterion: All operations are undoable and land on intended grid positions.

Steps: Load into Cue; confirm estimated BPM; enable stretch; launch with drum clip.
Expected result: Cue clip remains synchronized at session tempo with acceptable quality.
Pass criterion: User understands Cue sync works while local Warp Marker parity is absent.

Steps: Load clips into two rows; set one-bar quantization; launch scenes; stop one track.
Expected result: Clips start together on boundaries and individual track stopping works.
Pass criterion: No accidental Arrangement edits or global stop.

Scenario: Record directly into a clip slot
Starting state: Audio input configured; empty Cue slot
Steps: Arm cue recording; choose four bars; start transport; perform; let recording finish.
Expected result: Four-bar clip begins playing at the expected quantization boundary.
Pass criterion: Recorded material is audible, named and editable in the lower pane.

Scenario: Turn a cue performance into an arrangement
Steps: Enable Capture Performance; launch scenes for two minutes; stop; open Arrangement.
Expected result: Editable timeline representation reproduces the heard cue sequence.
Pass criterion: Playback after capture matches event order, timing and automation policy.

Starting state: Audio input and vocal track configured
Steps: Record three takes; show comping workspace; audition; assemble final take.
Expected result: Composite plays selected phrases with original takes recoverable.
Pass criterion: No extra manual tracks required; edits remain reversible.

Scenario: Create returns and mix from Arrangement
Steps: Create A Reverb and B Delay; add sends; adjust volume/pan/sends from right-side controls.
Expected result: Routing is correct and all mix controls update Ardour mixer state.
Pass criterion: No need to open full Mixer or routing grid for common operations.

Steps: Show automation; select cutoff; arm automation; record movement; stop; replay.
Expected result: Automation is written and replays; lane exits destructive Write state safely.
Pass criterion: Existing automation outside the touched interval remains intact.

Scenario: Commit a processed part to audio
Starting state: MIDI or audio region with processors
Steps: Select range; invoke Bounce with Processing; place result on audio track; compare.
Expected result: Rendered audio matches the processed playback and source remains recoverable.
Pass criterion: No silent, clipped or time-shifted render; original is retained.

Steps: Quick-export master; stem-export selected tracks with and without processing.
Expected result: Master and synchronized stems are created with documented format and processing.
Pass criterion: Files open, align at zero and contain expected processing.

Scenario: Apply and completely remove the profile
Steps: Install profile; make one profile change; restore backup/remove profile.
Expected result: Original keybindings, theme, templates and layout are restored without session loss.
Pass criterion: Hash/diff confirms unrelated user configuration is preserved.

Scenario: Confirm adaptive grid and magnetic snap after install
Starting state: Fresh Ardourton install; new or no-session editor state
Steps: Zoom from full-session to sample level; drag a region at several zooms; open Preferences → Editor → Snap; optionally check Cue MIDI clip editor.
Expected result: Grid switches from bar-level to individual-beat ticks only once beats are comfortably spaced (~70-80px apart) rather than while still cramped; drags pull within ~10px; Prefs show threshold 10; granularity 250; rulers-follow-grid on; Snap Target Both.
Pass criterion: Grid menu still overrides manually and adaptive behavior resumes after switching back to BeatDiv32/Magnetic.
Evidence to capture: Screen recording of zoom/drag; Prefs screenshot
